content.intro: This lesson belongs to Module 23: Production Hardening and Operational Security. It builds practical understanding of Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management with the syllabus subtopics retained below.
content.why_it_matters: Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management turns a security intention into evidence, an operational owner, and a repeatable control. Inventory and review dependencies, protect build and deployment permissions, preserve artifact traceability, detect exposed secrets, and verify the resulting release before promotion.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management can be understood through this sequence: Capture operational signal → Protect sensitive context → Assign accountable owner → Review and improve. Start with the application asset and trust boundary, state what secure behavior should occur, and identify the evidence that would prove or disprove it.

content_blocks.title: Connect the syllabus subtopics
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum groups this lesson around: 175.1 Dependency and framework lifecycle; 175.2 Migration away from unsupported components; 175.3 Secure decommissioning; 175.4 Credential, data, and artifact cleanup; 175.5 Final access revocation and audit records. Treat these points as a checklist, not a list to memorize: explain the risk, identify the root cause, select a control, and define a test for that control.

items.title: Scope
items.text: Identify the asset, principal, input, state, or boundary affected. State whether the example is local, owned, or explicitly authorized.

items.title: Control
items.text: Inventory and review dependencies, protect build and deployment permissions, preserve artifact traceability, detect exposed secrets, and verify the resulting release before promotion.

items.title: Failure behavior
items.text: Include an invalid, denied, expired, malformed, repeated, or otherwise relevant boundary case. Fail safely without exposing secrets.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Record expected versus actual behavior, a sanitized request or test result, the root cause, the chosen fix, and the regression test.

content_blocks.title: Safe reference example: Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management
content_blocks.code:
Topic: Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management
Review artifact: define scope, assumptions, control owner, expected secure behavior, failure behavior, and a reproducible verification step.
content_blocks.expected_output: A written review artifact names the control and the evidence needed to verify it.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a local/owned application or explicitly authorized test target. Record only sanitized synthetic evidence; use human review for behavior that a static snippet cannot prove.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a clean local test account and synthetic data. Reset the test fixture after recording the result; do not include credentials or private data in the course report.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not confuse an observation with proof or rely on a UI-only restriction. Inventory and review dependencies, protect build and deployment permissions, preserve artifact traceability, detect exposed secrets, and verify the resulting release before promotion. If evidence is ambiguous, reduce the test to one condition, inspect the application code/configuration, and repeat only within the permitted scope.

content_blocks.title: Execution and safety boundary
content_blocks.text: The current CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview, not a secure runner for arbitrary server code. This example is a static reference unless the run instructions explicitly identify a supported local environment. Use a private local lab or a test system with written authorization; do not test unrelated public systems.

content.task: For “Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management”, write a short security note or test in a local/owned application. Identify the expected secure behavior, at least one relevant failure case, and the evidence needed to prove the control works.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the core rule for Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management in your own words.
Name the trust boundary and the server-side control or policy that applies.
Specify a repeatable test for expected behavior and a relevant denied/failure path.
Use synthetic data and redact credentials, tokens, and personal information from evidence.
hints: Start by stating the asset, input, actor, or trust boundary and the expected secure behavior.
Change one condition at a time; record expected and actual outcomes with synthetic data.
Check the linked official reference for framework-specific settings and version-dependent behavior.
content.expected_output: A concise control explanation and a sanitized test record showing expected/actual behavior, one failure case, and a regression check.
recap: Secure Maintenance and End-of-Life Management is a security boundary/control topic, not a standalone checklist item.
Inventory and review dependencies, protect build and deployment permissions, preserve artifact traceability, detect exposed secrets, and verify the resulting release before promotion.
Retest fixes and record sanitized evidence; use only authorized environments.
